record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation u(t) = g(t) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds for t \ge 0, where g is continuous and bounded on \mathbb{R}_+. For which continuous or weakly singular convolution kernels k_0 and k_1 do all solutions satisfy \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t) = 0?

evidence.quote: The analysis of the asymptotic stability of numerical schemes—in particular Runge-Kutta and collocation methods—for solving VFIEs with vanishing delays ought to be based on the linear test VFIE u(t) = g(t) + ∫ t 0 k0(t − s)u(s)ds + ∫ qt 0 k1(t − s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0. (4.6)

Open Problem 4.1 (a) (i) Let g be a continuous and bounded function on R+. Which (continuous, or weakly singular) convolution kernels, k0 and k1, does the solution of the linear test FVIE (4.6) satisfy (4.2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a constant $q \in (0,1)$ and consider the linear Volterra functional integral equation with a proportional vanishing delay
$$u(t) = g(t) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)\, u(s)\, ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)\, u(s)\, ds, \qquad t \ge 0,$$
where $g:\mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ is continuous and bounded, and $k_0, k_1$ are convolution kernels that are either continuous on $[0,\infty)$ or weakly singular (i.e., of the form $k_i(\tau)=\tau^{-\alpha_i}\tilde{k}_i(\tau)$ with $0<\alpha_i<1$ and $\tilde k_i$ continuous). Characterize the pairs of kernels $(k_0, k_1)$ for which every solution $u$ of the above equation satisfies
$$\lim_{t \to \infty} u(t) = 0.$$
Provide necessary and sufficient conditions on $k_0$ and $k_1$ that guarantee this asymptotic decay, distinguishing between the continuous-kernel case and the weakly singular case.
artifact.category_tag: Volterra integral equations with vanishing delays
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has addressed asymptotic stability for the linear Volterra equation with vanishing delay in the case of general continuous convolution kernels, using a variation-of-parameters extension and energy estimates. However, the corresponding complete characterization for weakly singular kernels appears still to be unresolved, and the problem is consistently referenced as relevant to the still-open numerical stability analysis of collocation/Runge–Kutta methods for VFIEs with vanishing delays.

status_evidence.title: On the asymptotic stability of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Linear Volterra integral equations with general continuous convolution kernels and vanishing delays; asymptotic stability via an extension of the variation-of-parameter formula.
status_evidence.claim: Continuous-kernel case has been substantially analyzed, providing sufficient stability conditions.

status_evidence.title: Stability criteria for certain delay integral equations of Volterra type
status_evidence.snippet: Stability criteria are developed for delay Volterra integral equations.
status_evidence.claim: Related stability criteria exist but do not fully characterize the weakly singular case.

status_evidence.title: Cordial Volterra Integral Equations with Vanishing Delays
status_evidence.snippet: Studies cordial Volterra operators with vanishing delays.
status_evidence.claim: Weakly singular / cordial kernel analyses are ongoing, with full stability characterization not established.
